newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN AND PARMA EAGER TO AVOID MORE SLIP-UPS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN AND PARMA EAGER TO AVOID MORE SLIP-UPS.

text.p: Italian champions AC Milan meet old rivals Parma at the San Siro on Sunday in a game in which both sides need a good result after recent disappointing form.

Already eliminated from both the Champions League and the Italian Cup, Milan must obviously focus the rest of their season on an Italian title challenge, a point underlined by their Liberian striker George Weah.
"There's still a long road in front of us. We've been knocked out of the Cups and that's a pity but it's precisely because of that we must make the most of this situation.
"We ought to take advantage of being able to train right through the week without games in the middle".
Milan go into Sunday's game in third place, seven points behind in-form leaders Juventus and six points clear of Parma, who are currently fifth from bottom and just above the relegation zone.
Roberto Baggio, Marco Simone and Alessandro Costacurta are all ruled out of the Milan team through injury and illness.
Given those absentees, Milan coach Arrigo Sacchi may field an unusual tandem of Weah and Yugoslav Dejan Savicevic in attack, while Pietro Vierchowod steps in for Costacurta in defence.
Milan's poor season so far has already cost former coach, the Uruguyan Oscar Washington Tabarez his job. He was replaced by Sacchi at the beginning of the month.
Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti is likewise under pressure to hold onto his job following a dismal season which has seen Parma too eliminated from both the UEFA and Italian Cups.

Former Parma star Colombian Faustino Asprilla, currently with English club Newcastle United, scored the goal which gave Parma their only ever league win against Milan at the San Siro, a 1-0 victory in March, 1993 but he strikes a positive note about his old club.
"I have no doubts, Parma can win. I'd say that their difficult moment will soon resolve itself, simply because they have very good players".

Parma will be without two suspended defenders, Luigi Apolloni and Antonio Benarrivo, but still field a strong looking side featuring Enrico Chiesa and Argentine Hernan Crespo in attack with Croat Mario Stanic, Frenchman Daniel Bravo and Argentine Nestor Sensini in midfield.
Roberto Mussi and Fabio Cannavaro return in defence for Parma in place of Apolloni and Benarrivo.
